title: introduce-dependency-aware-rollback-plan-generator-and-rehearsal-mode
author: Aisha Patel
commits: 4 commits: (1) initial generator + DAG serializer; (2) helm hooks + migration hooks; (3) rehearsal runner + ephemeral-cluster script; (4) tests and docs; commit messages included in PR conversation
description:
Context and motivation: Private upgrades must be resilient across tenants, mixed Helm/Terraform changes, and multi-component dependencies (DB migrations, operator changes, config map flips). We observed two incidents where a naive post-failure rollback re-ordered steps and caused a cascading restart, increasing customer downtime (SUP-4382). This PR implements a dependency-aware rollback plan generator and a rehearsal mode that simulates the rollback in an ephemeral environment to surface ordering issues before committing.

What this PR delivers: - A rollback plan generator (installer/cli/rollback_plan/generator.py) that consumes the release manifest and a component dependency graph to emit a step-by-step rollback_plan.yaml with explicit ordering, preconditions, and safe-wait semantics. The generator tags steps that are safe to parallelize vs. strictly sequential. - A DAG serializer (graph_serializer.py) that snapshots current cluster relationships (K8s owners, Helm releases, TF managed resources) so plans are grounded in observed state, reducing mismatch during execution. - Helm chart hook templates (preupgrade-hook.yaml, postrollback-hook.yaml) to allow chart authors to register safe checkpoints; hooks are non-blocking by default and can be opted-in to enforce strict fencing. - Terraform module updates to surface a migration lock resource (pg-migration module) so the plan generator can detect ongoing logical replication/pg_upgrade activity and mark dependent steps as gated. - A rehearsal runner (operators/postgres/rehearsal-runner.sh + apply_rollback_plan.py) that spins up a throwaway namespace + ephemeral DB and replays the rollback_plan against the snapshot; failures are captured and surfaced as rehearsed-issues in the generated report. - Telemetry collector for rollback rehearsals (rollback_telemetry_collector.py) which records step duration, observed error classes, and an estimated blast-radius score used by the Console to prioritize manual review. - Integration tests and unit tests (installer/tests/test_rollback_plan.py) covering graph edge cases and serialization fidelity. - Documentation and an example playbook (installer/docs/upgrade-playbooks/dependency-aware-rollbacks.md) that explains how to use the new tooling and interpret rehearsal reports.

Design notes and constraints: - The generator intentionally prefers conservative ordering: if a step would touch a resource with active writes or an existing replication slot, it is marked "gated" and requires manual confirm or an automated quiesce. This avoids unsafe downgrades or partial schema reverts. - Plans include idempotency tokens and attempt counters so resume after a partial apply is safe; restore-step.sh contains guard checks (manifest hash, timestamp windows) to avoid accidental cross-release restores. - We keep execution separate from plan generation to support dry-run vs. execute modes. The rehearsal-runner uses the same planner but targets an ephemeral cluster to avoid touching production. - We added small, backwards-compatible Helm hooks; chart authors are not required to opt in, but opting in improves rollback fidelity for complex components.

Testing and CI: - Local unit tests cover graph reasoning and cycle detection. - End-to-end rehearsal runs are mocked in CI via an ephemeral KinD cluster; initial CI run failed due to a timing flake in rehearse runner (race in namespace teardown). I pushed a follow-up commit that added stronger waiting and the CI now passes. CI summary: 1 flaky test fixed; final status: passing.

Review conversation highlights (condensed): - Marco Chen: "Core idea LGTM, focus on making gating signals conservative — prefer human confirm over risky auto-revert." Author reply: "Agreed; default is gated/manual unless a config flag is set to allow auto-rollback for non-critical tenants." - Evelyn Ruiz: "We need audit traces for every step." Author reply: "Added per-step audit events with idempotency tokens; collector emits compact event blobs for Console ingestion." - Samir Gupta (SRE): "How does this interact with current restore playbooks?" Author reply: "generator can ingest existing restore manifests and will delta against them; added a compatibility shim in apply_rollback_plan.py." - Code owner approval from infra team after small adjustments to TF outputs and additional test coverage.

Migration/rollback playbook (how operators will use this): 1) Run: installer-cli generate-rollback --release vX.Y --output rollback_plan.yaml 2) Inspect: installer-cli rehearse --plan rollback_plan.yaml --report rehearsal_report.json (optional and recommended) 3) If rehearsal_report has no gated failures, run: installer-cli apply-rollback --plan rollback_plan.yaml 4) Monitor via Console; telemetry scores and per-step events provide visibility.

Backward compatibility and rollout: - This is additive: existing upgrade scripts remain unchanged and continue to work. - We patched Helm charts to include optional hooks; they are no-op unless chart author provides a hook script. - Terraform module changes export a new output (migration_lock_id) that older installers will ignore.

Release notes (short): Adds a dependency-aware rollback plan generator with rehearsal mode and telemetry, Helm hook support, Terraform module outputs for migration gating, and CLI commands to generate, rehearse, and apply rollback plans. Operators should run rehearsal for critical upgrades.

Follow-ups and TODOs: - Add a UI surface in Console to display rehearsal reports and blast-radius scores (tracked ENG-8810). - Expand rehearsals to multi-tenant scenarios with tenant-weighted simulation (tracked ENG-8822). - Add RBAC-aware plan generation so steps to restore secrets or KMS are separately gated (low-priority).

Files changed summary (high level): generator.py: new planner and policy rules; graph_serializer.py: snapshot utilities; helm template hooks: small YAML stubs and helper script; terraform: expose migration lock outputs and docs; rehearsal-runner: bash script + python runner; telemetry collector: lightweight event emitter; tests: new unit and e2e mocks; docs: new playbook and CLI usage.

Merge outcome: squash-merged into main after approvals from Marco Chen, Evelyn Ruiz, and SRE sign-off. This landed with CI green on 2024-10-16.
release_notes: Adds a dependency-aware rollback plan generator, rehearsal mode to simulate rollbacks in an ephemeral cluster, Helm hook templates for optional checkpointing, Terraform migration lock outputs, CLI commands to generate/rehearse/apply plans, and telemetry for rollback evaluation.
